sketches.mechanism: The __del__ destructor is never guaranteed to be called; objects may vanish without farewell when the interpreter shuts down.
sketches.resonance: Some goodbyes never happen — the language makes no promise that destruction will be witnessed.

sketches.mechanism: The 'object' keyword creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, enforced by the compiler.
sketches.resonance: Declaring something as truly singular means the language itself refuses to let you make another.

sketches.mechanism: Elm enforces pure functions with no side effects; the update function must return a new model, never mutating the old one.
sketches.resonance: You cannot change who you were — every version of yourself is immutable, and becoming someone new means constructing an entirely separate self.
sketches.draft:
type Msg = Tomorrow

update : Msg -> Self -> Self
update Tomorrow old =
    { old | age = old.age + 1 }

type alias Self =
    { age : Int
    , unchanged : Bool
    }
